implementation_statement: POL-02 (P06), approved 2026-09-21, replaces informal practice. It covers employees and the 140 contractor sales associates. Written procedures for contractor onboarding and offboarding are due 2026-11-30.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider; productivity suite; transaction platform vendor
implementation_statement: Employee accounts are created in the identity provider from HR onboarding tickets and federated to SYS-01, SYS-02, SYS-09, and SYS-10. Contractor agent accounts are created in the productivity suite directory and SYS-01 at a Sales Manager's email request, outside the single sign-on policy. Gaps: contractor accounts stay active up to 14 days after an agent leaves (8 of 12 sampled departures late); no quarterly access review; account types not documented.
evidence: IdP user export; contractor departure sample (12)

provider_if_inherited: Transaction platform vendor; closing software vendor; bank
implementation_statement: Each application enforces its own roles. SYS-02 is limited to the 7 Closing Services staff and the Controller. Online banking entitlements (SYS-08) are set by the bank to the Controller, one accountant, and Closing Services approvers. Cloud console access uses provider IAM roles for 3 named administrators.
evidence: SYS-02 user list; bank entitlement report; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: External automatic forwarding is allowed in the productivity suite. P07 testing found five contractor mailboxes forwarding to personal webmail (P01 R-032). Planned: block external auto-forwarding by transport rule and remove the five rules by 2026-09-30.

Wires from the title escrow trust account need a preparer and a separate approver with a hardware token. Wires from the sales and property management escrow accounts need only one approver (P03 G-051). Planned: dual approval on all escrow accounts by 2026-10-15.
evidence: Bank wire approval settings; P03 G-051 and G-057

implementation_statement: The transaction platform uses office-wide visibility, so each contractor agent can open every transaction in their office (about 70 agents per office). The 3 cloud administrators also administer the backup vault. MSP technicians share one administrator account. Planned: team-based visibility in SYS-01 by 2026-12-31; separate backup administration (P01 R-006); named MSP accounts (R-014).
evidence: SYS-01 role settings export; cloud IAM export; MSP account list

implementation_statement: Accounts lock for 15 minutes after 10 failed sign-ins in the identity provider and the productivity suite, including contractor accounts.
Company laptops and desktops lock after 10 minutes idle by device policy. Contractor personal devices are covered by AC-19 and AC-20.

Employees reach SaaS systems over TLS with single sign-on and MFA; both offices connect to the cloud tenant by site-to-site VPN. Gap: the MSP remote management tool is not restricted by source address and uses one shared technician account (P01 R-014).

No control over contractor phones and laptops that sync email and transaction files. Planned: mobile application management for the email and transaction apps (app-level wipe, no local attachment storage) by 2027-03-31 (P01 R-008).

Contractor agents use personal devices under the independent contractor agreement, which has no device or security terms. Planned: minimum device standard and security terms in the agent agreement at the 2027 renewal cycle.
Training requirements are set in POL-05 4.3 (approved 2026-09-21). No written training procedure or annual plan yet.

Employees watch a generic annual video. Contractor agents receive no training and there are no phishing exercises. Planned: BEC and wire fraud training for all employees and contractors, and quarterly phishing exercises, by 2026-12-31.

Closing Services staff learn wire procedures on the job. No role training on payoff verification, callback, or changed-instruction handling. Planned with the written disbursement verification procedure (P01 R-002) by 2026-10-31.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite; transaction platform vendor; cloud provider
implementation_statement: Mailbox auditing, sign-in logs, SaaS audit trails, and cloud management events are generated by vendor default. The company has not selected which events it needs (inbox rule creation, forwarding changes, bulk downloads, wire instruction edits in the portal).
Audit records include user, time, source address, and action, as provided by each SaaS service.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody reviews logs. There are no alerts on new forwarding rules, unusual sign-ins, or bulk downloads (P03 G-021). Planned: MSP alerting with a weekly review by the IT Manager by 2026-12-31.
Default retention only (as short as 90 days for some sign-in data). Planned: export to a log workspace with 1-year retention.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite; transaction platform vendor; cloud provider
implementation_statement: Log generation is performed by the SaaS and cloud services for all users.
First control assessment performed 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-28 by an independent assessor (P07). Annual assessment set in POL-01; not yet a recurring cycle.
Weaknesses from P03 and P07 are tracked in the POA&M (P07) with owners and dates. The COO reviews it quarterly from 2026 Q4.
No continuous monitoring. Planned: MSP-managed EDR with 24x7 alerting, monthly vulnerability scans, and monthly sampling of the callback procedure.

baseline: High (added by tailoring for the High integrity rating)
implementation_statement: No penetration test has ever been performed. Planned: external network and Closing Communications Portal application test by 2026-11-15, then annually, because the company does not have effective continuous monitoring.
Company laptops are built from the MSP standard image. No documented baseline for the firewalls, the integration service virtual machine, or the portal's platform configuration.

No change procedure. The contract developer deploys portal and integration changes directly to production (P01 R-029). Planned: change requests with test evidence and IT Manager approval by 2026-12-31.
No security impact analysis before changes. Planned as part of the CM-3 procedure; changes that touch wire instruction display require a second reviewer.

Employee sign-in policies are set in the identity provider. Gaps: legacy email authentication protocols remain enabled for all mailboxes, and the email domain's DMARC policy is set to monitor only (P01 R-004).
Firewalls expose no inbound services. Unused services are not reviewed on the integration service virtual machine, and personal devices can join the staff Wi-Fi (P01 R-030).
A spreadsheet lists SaaS systems and the 64 company laptops and desktops. Contractor devices, paper records, and the locations of customer information are not inventoried (P03 G-012).

The BIA (P05) sets MTD, RTO, and RPO for every process. No written contingency plan yet. Planned: contingency and hurricane plan built from the BIA, including a remote closing procedure, by 2027-05-31 (P01 R-022).
No restore test has ever been performed for the portal, the integration service, or email. Planned: quarterly restore tests starting 2026-12-31.

Daily backups of the SYS-05 workloads are stored in the same cloud account, managed by the same administrators. SaaS vendors keep their own backups; the company has no independent copy of email or transaction files (P01 R-006, High). Planned: separate account with immutable retention and third-party SaaS backup by 2026-12-31.
evidence: Backup job reports; vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: SaaS vendors restore their own services (transaction platform RTO 4 h and RPO 1 h per its SOC 2 report). The portal can be redeployed from the developer's code repository, but the steps are not documented or tested. The closing software vendor's recovery commitments are not documented (P05).
Every employee and contractor agent has a named account. Gap: the Main Office network storage device uses shared credentials, and MSP technicians share one account (AC-6).
evidence: IdP export; storage device user list

implementation_statement: Administrators of the identity provider, productivity suite, cloud console, and SaaS applications use MFA through the identity provider (authenticator app). The MSP tool also requires MFA.
evidence: Conditional access policy; admin role list

implementation_statement: All 60 employees use MFA for email, SSO applications, and the cloud console. The 140 contractor agents use a password only for email and the transaction platform (about 70% of users), and no written equivalent has been approved (P03 G-017, High). Planned: MFA for all contractor accounts and legacy protocol blocking by 2026-11-30.

Employee passwords are 14 characters minimum with a banned-password list in the identity provider. Contractor accounts follow the productivity suite default (8 characters). Local administrator passwords on laptops are managed by the MSP tool.

Buyers and sellers use the transaction platform client portal (vendor-managed accounts with email verification) and the Closing Communications Portal (emailed one-time code). The portal's one-time code goes to the same mailbox a BEC attacker may control. Planned: SMS or authenticator option for the portal after the penetration test.
evidence: Portal sign-in design; SYS-01 client portal settings

implementation_statement: POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-09-21.
No incident response training. Planned: role training for Closing Services, the Controller, and transaction coordinators on the BEC runbook, with the first tabletop exercise by 2026-12-15.
The BEC runbook (P08) has not been tested. First tabletop exercise due 2026-12-15, then annually (POL-03).

The BEC runbook (P08, approved 2026-09-21) covers detection, bank recall, IC3 reporting, containment, and notification. No runbooks yet for ransomware or lost devices. The March 2026 near miss was handled ad hoc and not documented.
Security events are not logged centrally. Planned: a Security category and incident log in the ticketing system by 2026-10-31.

POL-03 4.2 requires immediate reporting to the incident line. Contractor agents have no reporting instruction in their agreement or training, although their knowledge can start the FTC 30-day clock (P03 G-046).
POL-03 and the P08 runbook form the written incident response plan required by 314.4(h). Covers BEC only; other incident types are due 2027-03-31.
Paper closing files at the Branch Office sit in an unlocked storage room (P01 R-012). Planned: locked room with a key log by 2026-10-31.

A shredding vendor collects paper at both offices. There is no certificate of destruction for retired drives, and no retention schedule drives disposal (P03 G-018). The storage device will be destroyed with a certificate after its files are migrated.
Both offices are locked after hours with an alarm system; closing rooms are escorted. The Branch Office file room is unlocked and the storage device sits in an open area at the Main Office.
This SSP documents the TMCC boundary, categorization, and control implementation. Approved by the COO on 2026-09-21.
POL-05 Acceptable Use Policy approved 2026-09-21. Employees sign at hire; acknowledgments from the 140 contractor agents are not yet collected.

baseline: Not in any baseline (program management; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: POL-01 establishes the written information security program (approved 2026-09-21). Most program elements are defined but not yet operating (P03 G-001).

baseline: Not in any baseline (program management; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The IT Manager is the Qualified Individual, named in POL-01 4.2. The 2023 email designation has not been replaced by a signed letter stating authority and budget (due 2026-10-31).

baseline: Not in any baseline (program management; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are set in POL-01 4.4 and P01 section 1: the IT Manager accepts Low, the COO Moderate, and the majority owner High and Very High.

Employees in finance, escrow, and Closing Services pass a background check at hire. Contractor agents hold active state real estate licenses, which require a background check by the licensing authority.
Employee access is disabled the same business day from the HR termination ticket (4 of 4 sampled 2026 terminations on time).

Contractor agents are external personnel. Departures are noticed when the agent's license moves to another brokerage, and accounts stay active up to 14 days (P01 R-007). Planned: same-day disable and a weekly license roster reconciliation by 2026-10-31.
The employee handbook has a disciplinary process. The agent agreement allows ending the affiliation but does not name security violations. POL-01 4.7 now sets proportional sanctions for both.
First written risk assessment completed 2026-08-14 (P01, 34 risks, SP 800-30 Rev. 1 Tables G-5 and I-2). Reassessment each August (POL-01 4.3).
No vulnerability scanning has ever been done. Planned: monthly authenticated scans by the MSP from 2026-11-30, with remediation deadlines by severity.
Transaction platform and closing software contracts include security and incident notice terms. The tenant screening, MSP, and portal developer contracts do not (3 of 6 key contracts, P03 G-030).
The Closing Communications Portal was built in 2023 with no secure development standard (P03 G-015). Planned: a secure development standard in the developer contract by 2026-12-31.

No inventory of service providers that access customer information. The first SOC 2 report review was done in September 2026 for the transaction platform (P09). Planned: inventory, risk tiering, and annual reviews of tier-1 providers by 2027-03-31.
The portal has never been security tested. Planned: application penetration test by 2026-11-15, and developer testing evidence before each release.

Firewalls at both offices allow no inbound services; cloud network rules limit the integration service to the VPN range. Gaps: flat office network with the storage device reachable from every endpoint; no web application firewall in front of the portal; personal devices on staff Wi-Fi.
evidence: Firewall and cloud network rule exports

implementation_statement: SaaS services and the portal use TLS 1.2 or higher. Email uses opportunistic TLS; closing packages go out as unencrypted attachments unless the sender chooses encryption (P03 G-013). Planned: closing documents only through the portal, plus an enforced encryption rule for emails with Social Security or account numbers.
Commercial cryptography: TLS 1.2 or higher in transit and AES-256 at rest in the SaaS and cloud services, and full-disk encryption on company laptops. No FIPS 140 requirement applies to the company.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; device encryption report

implementation_statement: SaaS vendors and the cloud provider encrypt at rest; company laptops have full-disk encryption. Gap: the Main Office storage device holding 2016-2022 scanned closing files is unencrypted, and no compensating control has been approved by the Qualified Individual (P01 R-011).
Company endpoints patch automatically. The MSP patches the integration service virtual machine monthly. Firewall and VPN firmware is updated ad hoc (P01 R-010). Planned: quarterly firmware updates.
Signature antivirus on company endpoints; alerts go to an unmonitored mailbox. No EDR (P01 R-005). Planned: MSP-managed EDR with 24x7 alerting by 2027-01-31.
No monitoring of sign-in risk, mailbox rules, or bulk downloads. Planned: MSP alerting on these events and a weekly review (P03 G-021).
Basic spam filtering and an external-sender banner are active. Impersonation and look-alike domain protection are not configured, and DMARC is at monitor only.

No retention and disposal schedule; customer information is kept indefinitely. Planned: schedule reconciling the 314.4(c)(6) two-year disposal rule with Florida escrow and title record duties by 2027-03-31.
One supplier assessment completed (transaction platform SOC 2 Type 2 review, P09). No others.
